evidenceAudit.scope: Adults approaching kidney failure who are considering or have chosen conservative (non-dialysis) kidney management: shared decisions, symptom assessment, diet, anaemia and acidosis, and end-of-life planning. Verified against NICE NG107 and NG203; MOH Protocol-010 for symptom drugs; FDA labels for doses and contraindications.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Opioid choice in kidney failure — specialist

pathophysiology.summary: Conservative kidney management is planned, holistic care without dialysis for people with kidney failure, chosen when the burden of dialysis is likely to outweigh benefit (often older people with multimorbidity or frailty). The aim is to slow decline, control symptoms and plan for the end of life.
keyMechanisms: Falling GFR causes retention of fluid, potassium, phosphate and acid, and uraemic toxins (itch, nausea, fatigue, cognitive change).
Reduced erythropoietin causes anaemia; reduced phosphate excretion drives secondary hyperparathyroidism.
Symptoms may also arise from non-renal conditions — check before attributing them to uraemia (NICE NG107).

symptoms: Fatigue, breathlessness, itch, insomnia, poor appetite, nausea, cramps, restless legs, low mood, cognitive change (NICE NG107 Box 1).
physicalSigns: Oedema, pallor, weight change, signs of fluid overload.
redFlags: Potassium 6.0 mmol/L or more, severe acidosis or fluid overload — discuss goals and urgent options
Change in the person's wishes about dialysis
precipitants: Advanced CKD with frailty or multimorbidity

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Heart failure, depression, drugs — NICE NG107 1.1.4.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: eGFR around 5–7 mL/min/1.73 m² is where dialysis would usually be considered if asymptomatic (NICE NG107).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Keeps planning discussions timely; conservative care is reviewed if wishes change.

clinicalManagement.title: Shared decision
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At least 1 year before kidney failure is expected
actions: Start assessment for RRT or conservative management at least 1 year ahead (NICE NG107 1.2.1).
Offer a choice of RRT or conservative management; decide jointly, considering preferences, comorbidities and prognosis; revisit the decision (NICE NG107 1.3).

clinicalManagement.title: Symptom and complication control
actions: Renal dietitian assessment: fluid, sodium, potassium, phosphate, protein, calories (NICE NG107 1.7.1).
Phosphate binder (e.g. calcium acetate) if phosphate high; oral bicarbonate if eGFR below 30 and bicarbonate below 20 (NICE NG203).
Anaemia: iron (e.g. iron sucrose 200 mg IV, 5 doses over 14 days in non-dialysis CKD — label); epoetin if Hb below 10 g/dL per label.
Nausea and pain: see Nausea and Cancer Pain topics; start opioids low and seek specialist advice in renal impairment.

clinicalManagement.title: End-of-life planning
actions: Advance care planning; preferred place of care and death; anticipatory medicines (NICE NG31).

learningObjectives: Support shared decisions about conservative kidney management and control symptoms and complications.
